newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Feb 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Feb 19.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Interior Ministry is moving to unseat the attorney-general, claiming he overstepped the mark in dropping several high-profile cases that have caused a public backlash against the government. Kanit na Nakhon's most recent decision not to indict suspects in a case related to the Bangkok Bank of Commerce scandal, citing the expiry of the one-year statute of limitations, is understood to have prompted the ministry to act. (BANGKOK POST) (THE NATION)

- Burmese troops are poised to attack armed ethnic Karen soldiers in Chong Kamin as they inched their way towards the Thai border, some four kilometers from a southern village in Chumphon province. Chong Kamin is where the Karen National Union's 11th and 12th battalions are based. The attack is part of Rangoon's major military operation to secure control of the entire border with Thailand. (THE NATION)

- Faced with a sluggish economy, the government has come up with a new way to make quick money: a residence visa for any foreigner ready to invest 10 million baht in Thailand. It hopes to cash in on some 5,000 foreigners waiting to apply for residence visas, expecting at least 50 billion baht in foreign investment to pour into the country. (BANGKOK POST) + + + +

- The Bank of Thailand plans to ask banks to raise their capital bases to deal with non-performing loans and strengthen the soundness of the banking system, financial sources say. It remains unclear whether the banks will be required to raise their tier-one or tier-two capital to improve their balance sheets. (THE NATION)

- Speculation on the baht slowed yesterday after the Bank of Thailand released an official statement reiterating its stance that devaluation of the baht was definitely not a policy option to tackle Thailand's economic problems. The statement stressed that the baht was not fundamentally over-valued and said devaluation would cause more harm than good. (BANGKOK POST)

- The Association of Finance Companies has set up a sub-committee to come up with recommendations for finance firms interested in merging to establish two new commercial banks. The sub-committee will submit its conclusions to the Bank of Thailand for consideration next month. (BANGKOK POST)
